The bug is fixed: `![x\"x](x)` with `-x smarty` now gives `

`, the same as `![x"x](x)`. Nothing is committed. **Root cause:** a backslash escape like `\"` becomes a placeholder (`\x0234\x03`) while the text is parsed. The `UnescapePostprocessor` turned those back into real characters *after* the HTML was written out. So the serializer never got a chance to escape them, and a raw `"` ended up inside the attribute. Smarty makes this show up because it adds `"` and `'` to the characters that can be backslash-escaped. The same bug hit `attr_list` (`# a {: title="x\"y" }` → `

`) and link hrefs (`[a](x\"y)` → `href="x"y"`). Email autolinks with an escape came out garbled too. **Fix:** - **`markdown/treeprocessors.py`:** a new `UnescapeTreeprocessor`, registered as `'unescape'` with priority 0. It restores escaped characters in element text, tail text and attribute values before the HTML is written, so the serializer escapes them. - **`markdown/postprocessors.py`:** `UnescapePostprocessor` is no longer registered by default. The class is still there but now raises a `DeprecationWarning` when created, so third-party code using it keeps working. - **`markdown/extensions/toc.py`:** its `unescape()` helper now uses the new treeprocessor. - **`markdown/inlinepatterns.py` and `markdown/util.py`:** `Pattern.unescape` also restores escape placeholders, using a new `ESCAPE_PLACEHOLDER_RE`. This fixes email autolinks such as ``, which used to output the placeholder bytes as entities. - **`docs/change_log/release-3.4.md`:** notes on the deprecation and the bug fix. **One visible change:** an escaped `\>` in body text now renders as `>` instead of a raw `>`. Both are valid HTML; I updated the fixture in `tests/basic/backlash-escapes.html` to match. **Tests added:** - `tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_smarty.py` (new file): image alt, link title, link href and `attr_list` cases. - `tests/test_syntax/inline/test_autolinks.py`: an email autolink with an escaped character. - `tests/test_apis.py`: the new treeprocessor's behaviour, and the deprecation warning. **Test results** (`.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests --ignore=tests/test_syntax/extensions/test_md_in_html.py`): 677 passed, 4 failed, 129 skipped. The 4 failures are in `tests/test_syntax/blocks/test_html_blocks.py` and fail the same way without my changes. `test_md_in_html.py` has to be ignored because pytest can't collect it even on a clean checkout. Run with unittest, it shows the same 4 failures before and after the change. I couldn't run flake8 because it isn't installed in `.venv`.
